 Judgment

This is petitioners' appeal filed under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act')
seeking enhancement of compensation granted for the death of Ganesh the son of petitioners, in a motor vehicles accident dated 24.03.2017.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of petitioners that on 24.03.2017 Ganesh was proceeding in an auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.MH-25-M-0822 ('auto rickshaw' for short) from Honsal to Mardi.
It was driven by Malhari.

At 3:30 p.m. when the auto rickshaw was near the land of Kashinath Bhoge, situated side by Honsal-Solapur road, driver of the pick-up auto bearing Reg.No.MH-25-P-3535 ('offending vehicle' for short) came in a high speed, in a rash or negligent manner and dashed against the auto rickshaw.
As a result of the accident, both of them suffered grievous injuries and were declared as brought dead at the hospital.
As the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Respondent No.1 and 2 have filed separate written statement denying the averments regarding the age, occupation, income of the deceased, petitioners were dependent on him and that accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.
6. In respect of death of Malhari his legal representatives filed MVC No.354/2018.
Both cases were clubbed together and common evidence is led.
7. Petitioner No.1 (in MVC No.353/2018) is examined as PW.1, the father of Malhari (in MVC No.354/2018) is examined as PW.2.
Exs. P1
to 11 are marked.
8. No oral evidence is led on behalf of respondents, but Exs.R1 and 2 are marked on their behalf.

sentences.text: Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the petition and quantified the compensation at Rs.9,34,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same.

10. The details of the compensation granted are as under:
 Sl. Head Amount  No. awarded  1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,64,000/-
 2. Loss of love and affection Rs.40,000/-
 3. Towards funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 4. Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.

12. During the course of argument, learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the Tribunal has erred in considering the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- p.m. and failed to add future prospects.
The interest awarded also on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
13. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the records.
15.

Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the deceased died due to the injuries sustained in the said accident has attained finality.
16. Based on the evidence placed on record the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the deceased as 19 years and multiplier 18.
In the absence of proof of exact income, the Tribunal is justified in considering the income on notional basis.
Since the accident is of the year 2017, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.10,250/- p.m. instead of Rs.8,000/- p.m.
However, the Tribunal has not added any compensation towards loss of future prospects.

Since the deceased was aged less than 40 years, as per Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1, (Magma's case), 40% is required to be added towards loss of future prospects.

sentences.text: As parents of deceased, petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- each i.e., Rs.80,000/- under the head loss of consortium.
Therefore, compensation in a sum of Rs.40,000/- granted by the Tribunal under the loss of love and affection is disallowed.
The Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the head loss to estate and funeral expenses.

18. Thus, in all petitioners are entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.16,59,800/- as against Rs.9,34,000/- granted by the Tribunal with interest at 6% per annum as detailed below:
 Sl. Heads Amount awarded Amount  No by the Tribunal awarded by this  Court  1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,64,000/- Rs.15,49,800/-

2 . Loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- Rs.80,000/-
 (loss of love and  affection)

3. Towards funeral Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 expenses  4. Towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 Total Rs.9,34,000/- Rs.16,59,800/-
19.

To this extent, the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
( i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) Appellants/petitioners are entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.16,59,800/-
together with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.9,34,000/- granted by the Tribunal.

(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order together with interest at 6% p.a. (minus the compensation if already paid/deposited).
(iv) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
